key_insight: UEval is a focused benchmark of 1,000 expert‑curated prompts that require a unified model to generate both images and text, revealing evaluation gaps of simple LLM-as-judge approaches and enabling fine-grained assessment across real-world multimodal tasks.
problem_solved: Provides a standardized, expert-curated evaluation suite for unified multimodal generation (models that must output images + text), addressing the lack of benchmarks and the difficulty of reliably judging open‑ended multimodal outputs.
method: Curate 1,000 expert questions spanning 8 real-world tasks that explicitly require joint image+text outputs.
Design an evaluation protocol focused on multimodal reasoning types (step-by-step guides, textbook explanations, etc.) and highlight limitations of naive LLM-only judging.
Use diagnostic categories and human/expert validation to capture subtle multimodal correctness beyond simple automatic scoring.
impact: UEval enables rigorous, comparable assessment of unified models and drives development of better multimodal models and evaluation metrics, helping researchers identify strengths and weaknesses in how models combine visual and textual generation.

paper_title: UEval: A Benchmark for Unified Multimodal Generation
paper_authors: Bo Li, Yida Yin, Wenhao Chai, Xingyu Fu, Zhuang Liu
